To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the low-temperature asymptotics of the two-point functions of a spin chain can be computed by summing up a finite number of terms in the expansion into form factors, which is the main result of our paper.
the asymptotics of the correlation functions of the XX chain are described by a universal function, the so-called universal scaling function, which is a solution of the Painlevé II equation.

we have found a new method to compute the large-distance asymptotics for the transversal correlation functions of the XX spin chain, and have applied this method to obtain new results for the XX spin chain.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a fundamental question of statistical physics, namely the asymptotic behavior of the two-point correlation functions of a quantum integrable spin chain in the limit of large distance and low temperatures.
the asymptotic behaviour of correlation functions in the XXZ chain in the regime of large distances and low temperatures.
the low-temperature asymptotics of the two-point functions of quantum integrable lattice spin systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the asymptotic formulae derived in this paper are valid in the entire regime of low temperature and finite magnetic field.

the asymptotic formulae for the transversal spin-spin correlations in the XXZ chain are now known for all values of magnetic field, including the case of vanishing magnetic field, and for all distances, including the large distance case, with an exception of the saturation field, where the transversal correlations vanish identically.

the asymptotic formulae of the present paper are numerically efficient, and match well with existing results for vanishing magnetization and for short distances, and for low temperatures and magnetic fields below saturation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have derived the low-temperature asymptotic expansion of the correlation functions of the XX chain and its generalizations, which are of interest in the context of the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation, in terms of the asymptotically dominating terms of the expansion into form factors.
we give a complete answer for the low-temperature long-distance asymptotic behaviour of the transversally oriented two-point functions of all the XXZ chain with arbitrary anisotropy.
we have derived the low-temperature asymptotics of all the transversal correlation functions in the whole range of the coupling constant and the magnetic field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transversal correlation length of the XXZ spin chain is finite at all temperatures, even at zero magnetic field, in contrast to the ferromagnetic Ising chain.
the asymptotics of the two-point functions can be expressed in terms of a sum of the contributions of the form factors of a finite number of particles.
the asymptotics is governed by the asymptotically dominating form factors of the lowest-weight primary states, which can be computed using the algebraic Bethe ansatz.
